My Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Welcome back, Mrs Hocknell. We've reached tile 233 and we are, in time terms, about half an hour before [Baby N]’s second collapse on the day shift of 15 June, if you count the first collapse at 7.15 in the morning -- if you count the collapse at 7.15 in the morning as the first.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Anyway. This is a nursing note made by Lucy Letby, is that correct, timed at 13.53?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is this the actual time that Lucy Letby was making notes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's the update made on the computer, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we click on your transposition of the original, we see here that the note in total covers events at 07.30, after 08.06, after 08.40, 09.08 and at 11.00 hours. So those notes were all made at this time; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So otherwise, what you have produced here is nonspecific; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the remainder of the summary, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes. Could you read us through what Lucy Letby wrote, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Has remained cool throughout the day. Incubator temperature increased. [Respiratory] low, between 18 to 23 breaths per minute and shallow. Varying oxygen requirement of air to 40%. Mean cuff BP maintained. Initially tachycardic, now resolved. Perfusion and colour initially poor. 10ml/kilogram saline bolus given as prescribed. Remains pale/mottled but improved from earlier in shift. Nil by mouth. IV fluids (10% glucose) via peripheral line. Antibiotics given as prescribed.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Blood gases good, as charted. Infant stiff on handling and extending upper limbs, back arching. Settled in between episodes. Remains quiet. Urine not passed. Bowels opened: small green stool. Abdomen appears distended, soft to touch."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. So she was making that note, as you have recorded, at 13.53. Could we just look at the note itself, actually, so that we can be clear? And just get the time off the top.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This note is being made between 13.53 and 14.10; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we move to the next tile, 234, does it follow that these texts are being sent while she's updating the nursing notes on the computer?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: All right. So at 234, could you tell us what she sent to [Nurse E], please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Lol. I'll have 2 yogurts for tea, ha ha."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then a further message:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yeah, came not long after you left and both stayed since."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's in relation to the parents, I think.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes. Then did [Nurse E] respond:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hopefully will keep phones on in future."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then, at 237, did she make a note timed at 14.00 hours on the observation chart concerning [Baby N]’s heart, respiratory and temperature rates?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That too, if the timing was correct, would be whilst the nursing notes are open?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Ditto so far as the intensive care chart is concerned at tile 238?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And also the intensive care chart environmental checks data at tile 239?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 240, again, comes while those nursing notes are open. Can you tell us what she sent to [Nurse E], please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yeah, spoken to them about it. Mum left it upstairs or something and no signal, dad out driving to work."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 241 we have a further note that she makes concerning [parents of Baby N]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Could you talk us through that, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Parents have been present since. Both understandably upset. Support given and fully updated by myself, Consultant Saladi and medical team. Aware of support needed and plan of care. Mummy expressing, milk frozen."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did she then receive a message from [Dr A] on Facebook Messenger, timed at 14.32?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Does this read:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "It sounds like Serious Lucy did well to keep calm. I don't like faffing when there's a job to do either. Poor little thing is probably tired: he was handled lots overnight. Hope he can have a rest while the factor VIII settles the bleed."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There's material relating to a third party which isn't relevant followed by:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Only a few hours to go and it's holiday time for you. Do you think you'll manage to hand over quickly?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Was there then a further incident involving a collapse for [Baby N]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's marked by tile 243. If we go to 244, we see what Lucy Letby wrote about it; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did she write -- this is a note made later at 18.30, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did she write:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Approx 14.50 infant became apnoeic with desaturation to 44%. Heart rate 90 beats per minute. Fresh blood noted from mouth and 3ml blood aspirated from NG tube. Neopuff commenced and doctors crash called. Events documented in medical notes"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: The doctor concerned was a Dr Huw Mayberry from whom the jury will be hearing on Monday. Did he make a clinical note relating to his attendance as a result of a crash call?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's tile 245. At 246, did Dr Mayberry note what he encountered when he arrived?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 247, timed at 14.50, albeit it was a retrospective note made at 16.30, did Dr Saladi make a note concerning this event?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At tiles 248 and 249 do we have two bleeps, fast bleeps, to alert medical staff to attend at the neonatal unit, timed at 14.56 and 14.59?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, one for the neonatal registrar and one for Dr Saladi.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At 250, do we have some notes made by [Dr D] --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- from whom the jury will be hearing this morning, so I'll leave that for her to deal with, timed at 15.00 hours? I think she was the registrar; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 251, is there a note in the intensive care fluid requirements chart made by [Nurse B]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 252 was there a blood gas timed at 15.11?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, also made by [Nurse B].
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: You're speaking very, very softly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I could see you were struggling yesterday a bit. Have you got plenty of water there?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, the blood gas record is also made by [Nurse B].
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Then we have similar medications noted at 253, 254 and 255, as had been noted at about 8 o'clock that
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: morning, relating to elective intubation, is that right, for morphine, atropine and suxamethonium.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think those are dated for this event.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Oh, I know, but they're similar medications?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Similar medications, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So a repeat of the same sort of medications?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 256, part of Dr Saladi's retrospective note concerning the planning of an elective intubation, which was unsuccessful?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 257, Lucy Letby's own note concerning this event.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I would like to deal with that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Unable to obtain secure airway. Registrars [Dr D] and Mayberry, Consultants Brearey and Saladi unable to insert ET tube."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Do we then have, at 258, Dr Mayberry's clinical note concerning an unsuccessful intubation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by, going up the medical hierarchy, so to speak, the registrar [Dr D]’s note in similar terms and also recording the fact that Doctors Saladi and Brearey had been unsuccessful?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 260, is there a pharmacist's note --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- concerning the antibiotic cefotaxime --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- and indeed, factor VIII?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 261 is there a note made by Dr Saladi concerning the placement of a laryngeal airway by Dr Brearey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And then do we have, at 262, the first time we've seen this in this trial, a note made by some anaesthetists, who had been called to try to intubate [Baby N]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's Doctors Campbell and Jameson?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's timed at 15.50.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 263, is there a note on the fluid chart that is unattributed which records the 10% dextrose which was presumably being administered throughout this time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 264, also timed at 16.00 hours, the intensive care chart contains the usual data?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: This one signed or initialled by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 265, timed at 16.06, some swipe data recording the entrance of Lucy Letby into the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 266, timed at 16.15, observations charted by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 267, Dr Saladi's notes concerning his discussion with one of his counterparts at the Liverpool Women's Hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And also recording the fact that [parents of Baby N] were in the room and were regularly updated with clinical care?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 268, a note made by [Dr D] concerning an unsuccessful attempt to contact the anaesthetists?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 269 to 271, do we have the record made of the administration of those three drugs, morphine, atropine and suxamethonium, that we'd seen earlier --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- a few minutes ago, all timed between 16.40 and 16.48?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we then have two tiles, 272 and 273, untimed, but recording, first, the administration of the morphine and the suxamethonium and, secondly, the fact that the anaesthetists were having difficulty passing an ET tube?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 274, untimed but covering these events, do we then come to Lucy Letby's nursing note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I would like to deal with that, please. Does that say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Assistance gained from anaesthetic team x2 consultants. Also unable to secure ET tube. Intubation drugs given as prescribed. I-Gel airway inserted and infant ventilated via this. Secured with ties with vent hat. Nursed on CMV 18/4, rate 40 breaths per minute, inspiratory time 0.4. Oxygen variable. Currently requiring 50%. Blood gas good"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 275, is there a further note made by [Dr D] --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- concerning a communication with Alder Hey Children's Hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 276, timed at 16.55, is the time that the anaesthetists made their retrospective notes that we've already dealt with?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Sorry, we're not keeping up with this.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're still on 274.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm sorry, I took my eye off the screen.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 276 is the time at which the anaesthetists made their notes concerning their efforts to intubate [Baby N]?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. We then have three entries, all timed at 17.00 hours, between tiles 277 and 279. The first is the time at which Dr Mayberry made his notes, the second and the third are notes or data recorded by Lucy Letby concerning [Baby N]’s vital signs and his dextrose infusion.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 280 we have the third of what I have been calling, from time to time, the standard three, which is the NICU intensive care chart environmental checks, also completed by Lucy Letby, timed at 17.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We come next to an outgoing message sent by Lucy Letby to [Dr A]. To put this into context, [Dr A] had sent her a message at 14.32 saying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "It sounds like Serious Lucy did well to keep calm. Poor little thing, probably tired, he was handled overnight. Hope he can have a rest while the factor VIII settles the bleed."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Her response to that was what, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I'll still be here. He's poorly, bled again and became apnoeic. Steve, Murthy, Huw, [Dr D] and 2x anaesthetic consultants failed to intubate, so got an I-Gel in and awaiting NWTS with an ENT doctor. Sat having a quiet moment and want to cry. Just mad with so many people and lack of space, et cetera."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did she follow that a minute later?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Difficult times for you. Not sure what the answer is."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "OMG it's mad."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: To [Nurse E], that is.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes. Then [Nurse E] responded:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "What else has happened? Hoping it's just a clothing [that may be clotting] issue or something."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And Lucy Letby responded to her at tile 286, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Can't say much, just having quick toilet stop. Had anaesthetics and x4 consultants as can't get a tube. Waiting for NWTS with ENT specialist. [Query] trachy. Got I-Gel in."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did [Nurse E] respond, "Oh Jesus"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We then have at 288, timed at 17.35, a record of dexamethasone, followed at 17.45, tile 289, by a blood gas record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then [Dr A]'s response to the message or messages that he had received from Lucy Letby. This is tile 290, timed at 17.49.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did he respond:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Oh Lucy, poor little thing and you. It's it [that may be 'is it'] still chest or has he bled elsewhere? Huw [that's Dr Mayberry] texted to say there was swelling. Not sure if that's caused this or the result of attempts. Are you okay? Have a cry, you'll feel better for it I'm sure. You're welcome to take my car home if you're too tired to walk. I'll sort out picking it up in the morning. So sorry you had a rubbish day at the end of your long run. Holiday well and truly deserved."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And do we come next to clinical notes made by Dr Gibbs at 17.50, he will be coming to give evidence about that, followed by a further note made at 18.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We come next to the standard three at 293 through to 295, all timed at 18.00 hours and all recorded by Lucy Letby; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Then at 296, a long note made by Dr Saladi concerning a telephone call that he had received from one of the consultants at Alder Hey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Setting out in effect what the options were and those included transferring [Baby N] to Alder Hey --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- in Liverpool? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby then, at 18.19, send a response to [Dr A]'s Facebook message that had been sent at 17.49?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So this is 30 minutes later.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Blood from NG and mouth. Anaesthetics said severe epiglottitis [query] abnormal anatomy. Given dex. There was talk of a trachy but 2 doctors coming from Alder Hey Children's Hospital to assess shortly. Loads of input from different people, etc, so only just getting a clear plan. I'm okay. Just feel like I've been running round all day and not really achieved anything positive for him. Plus anaesthetic team were a bit rude and Minna and Bernie have been stressing, which doesn't help, along with being tired. Almost finished though. Don't want to cry in front of people here, maybe when I'm home! That's very kind re the but should be okay [it means about the car]. Have you managed to switch off at all and sleep?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Does she then send a message almost straightaway to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Losing the will."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And did [Nurse E] respond, "NWTS arrived"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. And Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "No, two consultants from Alder Hey Children's Hospital coming in car then will call for ambulance if needed as not sure long they will be, et cetera."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And [Nurse E] sends, "Poor little man".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we come next to tile 302, which is a nursing update made by Lucy Letby, some of which, the note that is, relates to events earlier which you have inserted at earlier stages in the chronology?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So far as the balance is concerned, would you help us with what the note said, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Infant has had periods of apnoea during the morning requiring stimulation and increased oxygen/PEEP. Improving by afternoon. Observations stable, remains cool so incubator temperature increased. X2 sodium chloride boluses given due to poor colour and perfusion. Mottled ++. Capillary refill remains 3 seconds. Colour has improved but remains pale with mottling to lower limbs. Infant quiet. Discussed sedation/pain relief and advised none required to number of previous drugs given and those that may be required. Dexamethasone given as requested by anaesthetic team via peripheral line (1st line flushing but leaking, 2nd line obtained). Fluids continue as previously.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Urine not passed. SBR remains below treatment line. CUSS carried out, NAD. Posture remains stiff and hypertonic. Medical team liaising with Alder Hey Children's Hospital re securing an airway. Awaiting arrival of ENT doctors who will assess infant. Factor VIII brought to unit by specialist nurse at Alder Hey Children's Hospital."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Then was that followed immediately by a family communication update note --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- at tile 303?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Parents present throughout the day and fully updated. Wished to be present for intubation attempts. Aware of need for airway and the different treatment plans that may happen, along with transfer to Alder Hey Children's Hospital. Upset but understand. Daddy has gone to collect items from home. Parents encouraged to sit with infant and to name him. Haemophilia. Nurse Cathy Benfield has visited the parents, number 07 [there's a telephone number], should we wish to contact her."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That may be "haemophilia nurse, Cathy Benfield".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 304, is that one of the ENT registrars' notes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 305, timed at 18.36, did Lucy Letby send a message to her mum?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Will be late off as got a sick baby and waiting for transport team to take to Alder Hey. Love you."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then, at 306, did the door swipe data record Lucy Letby coming into the neonatal unit entrance?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 307 did Susan Letby respond to Lucy:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Okay, love you too."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Was that followed at 308, timed at 18.41, by further door swipe data recording the passage of Lucy Letby through to the -- from the labour ward to the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We then have a message from [Dr A] to Lucy Letby, timed at 18.49 in the following terms:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "No, not really."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then some private content relating to a third party who's not relevant:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Your day sounds as though it's been horrible. Do you know when NWTS are coming or are they waiting for Alder Hey ENT first? I've never heard of epiglottitis in a baby. Odd then that his CRP was less than 1. The blood was obscuring my view of the cords. Sounds like there was an inflammatory thing going on which got worse. Poor you. Are you going to be okay? I'm sure he's had the best care possible today and that you will have done everything you can for him. Are you doing anything nice before you go on holiday? Torbay in a few weeks' time. You're

blocks.text: not having to do a long run of shifts to get the time off for that, are you? Take care."

blocks.text: We've heard that's a treatment for jaundice?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: That explains your next line:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's a bilirubin count?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: "... repeated at 9 am. Result 150. Lights stopped.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: For repeat in the morning."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So at 9 o'clock, you were able to cease that treatment; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: "Baby demanding bottle feeding on expressed breast milk."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do you recall that now?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do, from reading that, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: "Taking good amounts on own bottles. Baby very unsettled early part of the night."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do you remember anything about why he was unsettled in the early part of the night?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Nothing particular comes to mind.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: What do you think you mean by "the early part of the night"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's normally when we've taken over handover up to about 12 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And do the notes suggest he was unsettled when at first you took over?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: How did he do thereafter, do you recall?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was around 1 o'clock he started deteriorating a little bit. So he became a bit mottled, which is a blanching rash all down the body.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Before we get to 1 o'clock could I ask Mr Murphy to put tile 43 up, please. This is [Baby N]’s feeding chart which I'll ask you to have a look at, please. Do you recognise your handwriting (overspeaking) --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: I think I know which it is, but can you just tell us?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: 9 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Thank you. So it's the bottom entry, is it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So we've moved on to -- we're still on 14 June, it's 9 o'clock, expressed breast milk, 60ml, is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Given by bottle; yes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: That would be -- he's passed urine. Is that bowels not opened?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And just to clear something up from yesterday I think, N/B, is that a name band? Is that an abbreviation for name band?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So you have to confirm that the baby (overspeaking) --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They have to have two name bands on.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: In your comment box is that "demanded"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. So he's demanded a feed early.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So a little unsettled at the start of shift. 9 o'clock, he is demanding a feed and takes the feed of 60ml.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Would you have noted if he'd not taken it all?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I would have put a comment on the box to say he'd not taken it well.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Does the fact he was demanding a feed and took all 60ml, does that tell you anything about the baby at 9 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It just says that he's a well baby and was hungry.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: All right. You started to tell us about 1 o'clock -- I'm sorry, I interrupted and cut across. Tell us again what happened at 1 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think he started to look a bit more mottled, which is a rash down the belly, and was more unsettled than the start of the shift.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: What did you do in those circumstances?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Would you normally bring it to someone's attention?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I'd have normally told the shift leader.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: We know that the shift leader on that particular shift was Belinda Williamson?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you think you told Belinda Williamson?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I would have done, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. And was there a change, do you recall -- whoever you told, was there a change at that stage in [Baby N]’s monitoring?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Let's have a look, please, at tile 42. Look at the document behind, please. We know this is an observation chart.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: If we look across the top to the right we can see "15 June" in the date row. If we look down, it looks like, please correct me if I'm wrong, from 1 o'clock you started to monitor heart rate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And where would you get that particular reading from?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We'd have placed him back on to a saturation monitor.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Thank you. You're also monitoring, as we scroll down, his respirations, so no need to do them up until then, but because of what you saw, some additional attention given --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: -- to [Baby N]? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So from 1 o'clock onwards, do you recall how [Baby N] fared for the rest of the shift thereafter?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He started to deteriorate from 1 o'clock. I'm not sure about times but he did start to have a few desaturations, which is when we would have commenced full monitoring, to keep an eye on him, and he would have had a septic screen and antibiotics.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Shall can we have a look at your note again. Maybe that's the best way. 78, please, Mr Murphy. Quite right:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I noticed that, just after 01.00 feed, baby looked very pale."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So he was fed -- there isn't a feed on the feeding sheet at --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It wouldn't have been on that one, it should have been the one after.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So he'd just fed. Started to look pale mottled and veiny. His abdomen slightly bigger. Seen by NNU Nurse Belinda Simcock as she was then, and advised, as you rightly said, to place on saturation monitor:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Reviewed by paeds."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Would that be the doctors (overspeaking) --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That was [Dr A], yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Thank you:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "To be watched for an hour. After 30 minutes noted to be having desaturations to low 80s. No intervention required but quite frequent."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just tell us why there would be no intervention?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That means he would have corrected himself, he would have come up before we'd gone in to --
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: All right. We've also heard that sometimes it's enough just to tickle the feet or give the baby a shake?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: "Rest of observations within range."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Which we just looked at:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Reviewed by [Dr A] and for septic screen. Cannula inserted into right hand. Bloods taken for CRP, blood culture and..."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think that's full blood count; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. Is that, "IM CF given by NNU nurse"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's IM cefotaxime given; that's an antibiotic.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Started on antibiotics and as you're a nursery nurse it's an NNU nurse that comes --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't give any medication.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: -- and does that? Okay:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Baby looked worse this morning and cap refill was 3 seconds."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We've heard that's a process where you press your finger on the baby and count how long until the colour recovers; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: "Reviewed again by paeds. Placed into 25% Oxygen ambient [is that] and nil by mouth"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's when the oxygen's going round the incubator.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So we've heard about various forms of ventilation.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is that simply gas being blown into the incubator itself?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Thank you:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "10% dextrose commenced [on that particular rate]. Cannula site satisfactory. Passed urine, bowels open."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: At 06.02 you have noted that at that stage there hadn't been contact from the parents?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Thank you. Just look -- you mentioned blood gases so if we can just look at the blood gases, please, at tile 79.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can scroll down, I think you're pretty well in the middle with the darker script; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Are they your initials?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: We can see bloods at 01.27 and 03.41, both capillary samples. You may be asked some questions about those but you simply observe [Baby N] was self-ventilating in air?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't interpret blood gases; I can just take them.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: All right. Your note spoke of him going on to glucose.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: -- sorry, a dextrose infusion. Did he go -- was he placed nil by mouth at that stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He was, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: That was following [Dr A]'s septic screen, was it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: If we can just look at the infusion chart, please, at tile 110.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do you recognise the handwriting on the chart there to the left?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Is that yours?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So it looks like, please correct me if I'm wrong, that infusion started at 5 am?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was 5.30. I think I've wrote underneath 5.30.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Yes, I'm glad you did correct me. Putting again together that sort of timeline, you've got the two blood tests and the glucose starting at 5.30?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Between 5.30 and handover, or just before handover, how was [Baby N] after that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He'd settled down once we commenced the fluids but from about 7 o'clock onwards he was having more desaturations.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember when the desaturations started?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't, sorry.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember any of the desaturations in particular?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Only when he had a big one at about quarter past 7.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. So he had a big one about quarter past 7. Do I infer from what you said there'd been some before or after that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I don't think they needed much intervention though.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Are we talking about the self-correcting ones that you mentioned to us a little earlier in your evidence?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Tell us about the big one at 7.15?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember it in full detail. I remember Lucy looking over and he'd gone a bit pale because his monitor had gone off. I think we then started Neopuffing.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Which room was this in?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Nursery 3.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So we know [Baby N] started in nursery 3 from the plan that we saw. Even though he had been placed nil by mouth, no decision to move him at that stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, we wouldn't have moved him because he'd settled down a bit.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So not sufficiently poorly to have to move?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, because he didn't require any respiratory effort.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And of course you continued to be his designated nurse, there was no escalation to one of the NNU nurses?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, Belinda Simcock was aware of what I was doing.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So it's in room 3 and it's about quarter past 7. Do you remember what you were doing at the time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't have a distinct memory. I just think I was feeding a baby.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. We saw the other -- perhaps if we could go back to the tile with the plan of the room on, tile 37, please. Use that. If we could enlarge it again, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So one other baby in nursery 3 on the shift, unless someone else had been brought in. Do you remember anyone else coming in during the course of the night being added?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So you think you were feeding the other baby in the room?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think so.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. Looking at our plan, perhaps we could zoom in a little bit on nursery 3, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not very scientific, but do you remember looking at the nursery where [Baby N] had been in his incubator?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I wouldn't remember where he was.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember where you were when the baby, I should say, you were feeding was when this happened?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: All right. How were you feeding the baby?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: We've heard there can be bottle, there can be the nasogastric tube where it's put in and it drips through by way of gravity. Do you remember which one it was?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: What makes you think you were feeding a baby?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just because I know I was in the room at the time and I would have gone over to the monitor had I not been doing anything.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. So you're feeding the baby. Tell us what happens next, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think the monitor went off, so Lucy went over to see and he looked quite pale and I think had kind of stopped breathing. She got the Neopuff and I went over to help.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: It's 07.15, do we take it from that that Lucy was there at that stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember when she'd come in?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was about 10 past, quarter past 7.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And do you remember what she was doing or where she was when this happened?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: She'd just come in to say hello.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: When you heard the alarm go off, did you look over towards [Baby N]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I did, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And do you remember where Nurse Letby was at that point?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: You don't. Was she in the room?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Okay. Was anything said?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember which alarm it was that was sounding?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't, no.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: When you looked over, did you notice anything about [Baby N]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Let's have a look at your note of this incident, please, before we go too much further. Tile 141, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it's probably towards the bottom left of our screen, if I recall rightly, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So your note at the time says:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 07.15 baby crying and dropped saturations. Seen by NNU Nurse Lucy."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Does that remind you of the sequence of events?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Some, not all.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: You haven't mentioned the alarm in there. What do you mean by "seen by Lucy"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: She would have seen the monitor so she would have seen the drop on the saturation monitor.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Presumably you'd heard the alarm by then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I would have thought so, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: When you -- just before we go any further, that's a note made at 08.19; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: I've asked you where Lucy was in the room. Had there been any conversation with you -- between the two of you before this particular incident?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: No? All right. Do you remember why she had come into the room?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just to say hello because we were friends.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Had she said hello by that point?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think so.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Had you been feeding the baby when first she came in, do you remember?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: You can't remember what you did. So the alarm goes off, you look over, you see that [Baby N] is, as you've noted there, mottled all over his body and blue; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And cold to the touch?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So when you saw that, where were you when saw that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'd have gone to his cot then.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: When you got to his cot do you remember where Lucy Letby was?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think she was next to me.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Who got there first; can you recall?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Lucy was there first.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you remember her moving across the nursery to get there?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Alarms go off. Did either of you say anything when you saw, in particular, the colour that [Baby N] had gone?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember the conversation.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: None at all? Do you remember what happened next?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I know we Neopuffed and then we decided to transfer the baby to nursery 1, which is ITU.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So bearing in mind that [Baby N] had stayed in nursery 3 through the night, was it considered there'd been a significant change at that point?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: What was that? Just cast your mind back if you can.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just because he needed Neopuffing, so he would have required respiratory support.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: And this was the first time it had gone that far?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: You put there:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Decision made to transfer to nursery 1. NG re-sited in right nostril."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is that the NGT, the nasogastric tube?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. We'd have put one in to empty his tummy.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: I beg your pardon?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We'd have put one in to empty his tummy.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Right. Do you remember when that was done?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: No? It says "with acid reaction". Just explain that to us.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We just have to test it to make sure we got a pH reaction, so the tube's in the right place.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So at that point the tube's gone in?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Someone's -- do you remember who it was aspirated the tube?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was me.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Is that what you would hope to find, the acid in the aspirate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: So it was in the right place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: There's a large file in front of you, I'm just going to ask you if you can go near the back of that, the very last tabbed document, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, these are the NNU reviews if anyone wants to follow this. I know it's a bit bulky, but it's the NNU review for this particular occasion.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If everyone's got the last one, please, if I can ask you -- have you got that last tab?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The green one?
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: That's it, yes. Go to the second page, thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Again, you'll remember that we've got our layout of the unit at the start. If we then, please, turn to page 4 of 13, we should see some rows at the top of the page and a couple of plans below. Yes? Everyone got that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The top box shows the population of the NNU at the end of the night shift. Do you see that? If you look at the plan, not the one at the bottom of the page, the one in the middle of the page, it looks very similar to the one we looked at on the screen, but this one actually represents what happened -- how things were at the end of the shift. If we look into nursery 3, it looks like it's got busier for you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: We can see there that, admitted at 21.00 hours and 02.00 hours respectively, are babies AH and AS; can you see that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Does that assist you with who you may have been feeding?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Does that ring any bells?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It does not at all, no.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY

blocks.text: Do you actually remember more babies coming in that night --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I don't, no.
blocks.speaker: JONES-KEY
